sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) is a vasoproliferative disorder of the developing retina in preterm infants. The distinction between 'Threshold' and 'Prethreshold' was established by the CRYO-ROP study to determine the necessity of ablative therapy (cryotherapy or laser) to reduce the risk of unfavorable anatomical outcomes (retinal detachment).

rows: Zone I any stage; Zone II Stage 2 with plus disease; Zone II Stage 3 without plus disease; Zone II Stage 3 with plus disease.
At least 5 contiguous or 8 cumulative clock hours of Stage 3 ROP in Zone I or II, in the presence of Plus disease.

sections.title: Risk Factors: The 3 'B's
content: Low Birth Weight (<1500g)
Low Gestational Age (<30 weeks)
Prolonged Supplemental Oxygen Exposure
Sepsis / Intraventricular Hemorrhage
Fluctuating SpO2 Levels

sections.title: Pathophysiology: Two-Phase Process
content: Phase 1: Hyperoxia-induced vaso-obliteration (loss of VEGF/IGF-1 signaling).
Phase 2: Hypoxia-driven neovascularization (VEGF upregulation leads to abnormal vessel proliferation).

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Treat Immediately
content: Presence of Plus Disease (venous dilation and arterial tortuosity in the posterior pole).
Stage 3 ROP in Zone I (Aggressive ROP/AP-ROP).
Tunica vasculosa lentis remnants.
Pupillary rigidity/poor dilation despite atropine/phenylephrine.

content.explanation: To meet Threshold: 5 contiguous clock hours OR 8 cumulative clock hours of Stage 3 + PLUS disease.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Serial screening (Indirect ophthalmoscopy) per ETROP guidelines.
Step 2: Identify High-Risk Prethreshold.
Step 3: Monitor vs Treat: Threshold disease requires intervention within 72 hours.
Step 4: Ablative Therapy (Laser photocoagulation is gold standard).
Step 5: Anti-VEGF (Intravitreal Bevacizumab) as adjunct/primary in select cases (e.g., Zone I).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Threshold disease represents the clinical 'point of no return' for high risk of retinal detachment.
ETROP study showed earlier treatment of 'High-Risk Prethreshold' (Type 1 ROP) improves outcomes.
Always document the Zone (I-III) and Stage (1-5) clearly.
Post-treatment: Monitor for 'reactivation' of neovascularization, especially after anti-VEGF injections.
